title: WPSS/3201/2017 of Arjun Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 3201 of 2017 (S/S)
Arjun Singh .....Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ....Respondents
Present :
Mr. Alok Mahra, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Vikas Pande, Advocate for respondent No. 6.
Mr. Praabhat Bohra, Advocate for respondent No. 5.

Dated: 25th April, 2019
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 An advertisement was issued on 1st February, 2014,
by the Director, Primary Education, Uttarakhand, whereby,
applications were invited from the eligible candidates for
recruitment on the post of Assistant Teachers, Primary Schools.
2. Primarily, the issue, with which, we are concerned in
the present case is in relation to as to what interpretation is to be
given to Clause (1) of the said advertisement dated 01.02.2014,
which relates to the qualification required by the candidate, which
as per the advertisement, reads as under :-

3. The said provision aforesaid provides that in order to
make a candidate eligible to participate in the process of selection
for the recruitment as an Assistant Teacher, Primary School, he or
she ought to be graduation as well as should have B.Ed. degree
issued from an institution which has been established in
accordance with the prevalent Indian Law and simultaneously, it
should be a qualification given by an institution, which is duly
recognized by NCTE as well as by the UGC.
4. On a composite reading of this Clause, when the two
qualifications have been made essential and as to be the basis for
eligibility to enable the candidate to participate in the selection, it
has had to be a qualification which is imparted by the Institution,
which has been established by Law as applicable in India.
5. Admittedly, as per the pleadings and records placed
by the petitioner before this Court, shows that he had completed
his B.Ed. qualification from an Institution called as "College of
Education, Kathmandu, Nepal", from where, he has been awarded
the degree of B.Ed., which has been issued to him from the
University called as "Tribhuwan University, Kathmandu, Nepal".
6. The petitioner was not considered and granted
appointment on the ground that the qualification which he posseses
in relation to the B.Ed. qualification, since being a qualification
which was imparted to him by an Institution established as per the
laws applicable in Nepal, the same cannot be treated as to be an
equivalent qualification as provided under Clause (1) of the
advertisement dated 1st February, 2014, and his B.Ed., which he
has completed from the Tribhuwan University, Kathmandu, Napal,
cannot be said to be a University, which is established as per the
laws applicable in India. On this premise, his candidature cannot
be treated as to be an eligible candidate entitling him for his
participation in the process of selection or consequent thereto for

3
the grant of appointment on selection in pursuance to the
advertisement dated 1st February, 2014.
7. Agitating his claim for appointment, the petitioner had
approached earlier before this Court by filing a Writ Petition, being
Writ Petition No. 2335 of 2015 (S/S), which was disposed of with
the direction to the respondents to consider the claim raised by the
petitioner for appointment by way of filing of a representation.
The same was disposed of by this Court by the judgment dated 10th
April, 2017, with the direction to take a final decision on the
representation in view of Annexure No. 8 dated 11th February,
2010, and the following order was passed :
"Accordingly, writ petition is disposed of with a
direction to the respondents to take a final decision in view
of Annexure No.8 dated 11th February, 2010 read in
conjunction with Annexure No. 13 dated 21.10.2014 within
a period of eight weeks from today."
8. On considering the aforesaid claim in the light of the
direction issued by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in its
judgment dated 10th April, 2017, the respondents considered the
case of the petitioner and had rejected the same by the impugned
order dated 24th May, 2017, which is under challenge before this
Court.
9. After having gone through the reasoning which has
been assigned in the impugned order, this Court is in agreement
with the reasoning given therein. Because the provisions pertaining
to the qualifications, as provided in the advertisement which
contemplates a graduation as well as B.Ed., to be essential
qualification for appointment as a Primary School Assistant
Teacher, it has had to be read that both the qualifications of
graduation and B.Ed. ought to have been acquired by the candidate

4
from the Institution or the University, which is duly established in
accordance with the law as applicable in the country.
10. Admittedly, the University from where the petitioner
has completed his B.Ed., since cannot be treated to be established
in accordance with the Indian Laws, the qualification acquired by
the petitioner from the said University cannot be treated as to be an
equivalent qualification to have been imparted by the institution
established under the Indian Laws.
11. Hence, I do not find any valid reason to interfere in
the impugned order. Consequently, the Writ Petition fails and is
accordingly dismissed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 25.04.2019
